name: Can an old pool be removed without damaging the rest of the yard?

mainEntity.name: Can an old in-ground pool be removed without destroying the lawn, trees, pavers, or irrigation around it?
mainEntity.text: Can an old in-ground pool be removed without destroying the lawn, trees, pavers, or irrigation around it?

acceptedAnswer.text: A careful contractor can limit damage, but pool removal always involves some disturbance to the yard. The difference between a rough job and a well-managed one is planning. Protection mats, small equipment, staged demolition, and clear access routes can reduce damage to existing landscaping, hardscape, and irrigation. Tree roots, sprinkler lines, lighting, and decorative pavers are especially vulnerable. In high-end neighborhoods across Los Angeles, homeowners often want the yard preserved as much as possible, which makes the contractor’s method just as important as price. Before starting, ask what areas will be protected, whether irrigation will be mapped, and how the contractor will restore the site after backfill. Some damage is common, but a good crew should limit it and clearly explain what will need repair after the pool is gone.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but only if the contractor plans for protection before demolition starts. The crew may use mats, smaller equipment, hand work, and staged haul-off to reduce damage to lawns, trees, pavers, and irrigation systems. Some restoration is often needed afterward, even on careful projects.
